Before You Go

Visa, money, phone data, weather and plugs: everything to sort out before you fly.

Visa & entry

Indonesian passport holders need permission before entering Taiwan. There are two routes.

A. Online TAC

Travel Authorization Certificate. Free, online, tourism only. Valid 90 days; stay up to 30 days.

Apply for the TAC (official)
Who can apply (Bureau of Consular Affairs)

B. Visitor visa

If you do not meet the TAC conditions, apply for a visitor visa at the Taipei Economic and Trade Office in Jakarta, before you travel.

TETO Jakarta (official)
Bureau of Consular Affairs

TAC basic requirements

  • Passport valid for at least 6 months from arrival
  • A return or onward ticket
  • Never worked as a blue-collar worker in Taiwan

And one of these

  • A valid visa or residence card (or one expired less than 10 years ago) from Australia, Canada, Japan, Korea, New Zealand, a Schengen country, the UK or the US
  • A Taiwan visa or residence card from the past 10 years with a clean record
  • A valid Japan Visa Waiver Registration
Apply earlyIf you are not eligible for the TAC, a visa takes time. Rules may have changed since the official page was last updated (2023), so confirm on the official sites above.

If required, also complete the online arrival card: arrival card.

Jamie's Corner

Fun fact

You don't see NT$200 and NT$2,000 bills very often in Taiwan, so if you happen to get one, you should keep it as a little treasure! 😆

Carry cashNight markets, small eateries and breakfast shops mostly take cash only. Cards work in malls, hotels and larger restaurants. ATMs at 7-Eleven and FamilyMart accept most international cards.

Tipping culture

  • Tipping is not expected in Taiwan.
  • Restaurants and hotels often add a 10% service charge to the bill.
  • Taxis: no tip. Rounding up the fare is welcome but optional.
  • Night markets and street stalls: no tip. A smile and a 謝謝 (xièxie) is plenty.

SIM & eSIM

Buy on Klook

Klook sells a Chunghwa Telecom eSIM for Taiwan with island-wide coverage. Install it with the Klook app or a QR code.

Klook Taiwan eSIM

  • eSIM: about NT$400–900 for 7–8 days. Check that your phone supports eSIM and is unlocked.
  • Airport SIM card: about NT$450–500 for 7 days, but counters usually close from midnight to 6 a.m. After immigration and baggage you may arrive too late, so the eSIM is safer.

Power plugs

Taiwan uses 110V / 60Hz with Type A and Type B sockets (flat pins).

Bring an adapterIf your plugs have round pins, bring a flat-pin adapter. Most phone and laptop chargers accept 100–240V, so check the label. Hair dryers and curling irons may not work well at 110V.

Final checklist

Transportation

Taipei is easy without a car. The MRT goes almost everywhere, with buses and taxis filling the gaps.

Airport to the city

Taoyuan Airport (TPE) is about 40 km from central Taipei. Check your terminal (T1 or T2) on your ticket.

OptionCostTimeGood to know
Airport MRT (purple line)NT$16035–40 min to Taipei MainBest choice. Last trains vary by train type and terminal, roughly 22:40–23:35. Confirm on the Taoyuan Metro site.
Bus (Kuo-Kuang 1819 and others)about NT$140about 60 minRuns 24 hours. Drops near Taipei Main Station.
Taxi / UberNT$1,100–1,500about 50 min24 hours, door to door. Fine with luggage or after the last train.
Your arrival: 21:00Immigration and baggage usually take about an hour. Aim for the platform by 22:15; if you might miss the last train, go straight for the bus or a taxi.

Airport MRT, step by step

  • Follow the purple "MRT" signs. Buy a token or tap an EasyCard.
  • Take the Express, not the slower Commuter train.
  • Get off at A1 Taipei Main Station. Changing to other MRT lines means a 10–15 minute walk underground.

Getting around Taipei

MRT (metro)

from NT$20about 06:00–24:00

Clean, frequent, with English signs. Lines are named by color and station code (R = Red). No eating or drinking in stations or trains. Stand on the right of escalators.

Taipei MRT map

Map: Taipei Rapid Transit Corporation. Check the official site for the latest version.

Bus

from NT$15

Pay with EasyCard. On most routes, tap when you board and again when you get off. Needed for the National Palace Museum and Yangmingshan. Google Maps shows live times.

YouBike

about NT$10–30 per hour

Rental bikes: pick up and return at any dock. Register through the YouBike 2.0 app with a credit card. Good for short, flat hops; skip it in rain or on mountain roads.

Taxi / Uber

base fare NT$85

Yellow taxis use a meter and can be waved down. The Uber app also works. Show the driver your destination in Chinese. Short city rides are about NT$100–250.

High-speed rail (HSR)

Taipei–Taichung about 1 hr

Useful for day trips to other cities, not needed for this itinerary. Taipei–Taichung is about NT$700. Stations: Taipei Main and Taoyuan (A18 on the Airport MRT).

EasyCard (悠遊卡)

about NT$100, non-refundable20% off MRT

A tap-to-pay card for MRT, buses, YouBike and convenience stores. Buy and top up at any MRT station or 7-Eleven. Start with NT$300–500.

Private car charter

Chartered 7-seat van with driver

7 seatsNT$4,000–4,600

A private van with a driver, good for day trips such as Jiufen, or when you have luggage and children. Prices are for the whole car, not per person.

HoursPricePer person (7)
6 hoursNT$4,000about NT$571
8 hoursNT$4,600about NT$657

The 8-hour option fits the Jiufen at dusk plan (leave around 11:00, back around 20:00).

Book: Taiwan Tour Car

Early departure: Dec 28, 09:10

Be at the airport by 06:30–07:00.

  • Safest: pre-book a taxi or Uber the night before and leave by 05:00–05:30.
  • Airport MRT: the first train from Taipei Main A1 is about 06:00, arriving around 06:40. Works if you stay near Taipei Main.
  • Bus 1819 runs 24 hours. Check the first bus time the night before.

Sights

Landmarks, mountains, street walks and night markets in Taipei.

Main attractions

Taipei 101 (台北101)

NT$600–650 observatorySkyline 460 combo NT$980about 09:00–22:00 (check)1.5 hours

A 101-floor landmark with an indoor observatory on the 89th floor and a mall below.

Getting there: MRT Red Line to Taipei 101/World Trade Center, Exit 4.

Tip: Book online to skip queues. Go about an hour before sunset (around 17:10 in December) to see daylight and city lights.

Freeabout 09:00–18:00 (check)1 hour

A white-and-blue memorial with a huge plaza, gardens and a changing-of-the-guard ceremony.

Getting there: MRT Chiang Kai-Shek Memorial Hall Station, Exit 5.

Tip: Watch the guard change on the hour. The plaza is great for photos.

National Palace Museum (故宮博物院)

NT$350Tue–Sun 09:00–17:00Closed Mon2–3 hours

One of the world's great collections of Chinese imperial art, including the Jadeite Cabbage and the Meat-shaped Stone.

Getting there: MRT Red Line to Shilin, then a 15–20 minute bus (Red 30, 255 or 304) or taxi.

Tip: Arrive at opening time to beat tour groups.

Open in Google Maps

Presidential Office Building (總統府)

Free1 hour

A red-brick colonial landmark from 1919 with a 60 m tower, now the office of Taiwan's president. The plaza in front is a favorite photo spot.

Getting there: MRT Red Line to NTU Hospital Station, then about 10 minutes on foot. Taipei Main Station is also close.

Visit the Presidential Office Building

Admission is free!

  1. Opening hours
    • Weekdays (Mon–Fri): 9:00 AM–12:00 PM (last entry 11:30 AM)
    • Selected Saturdays: usually 9:00 AM–4:00 PM. Check the official website for opening dates and hours.
  2. Visitor information
    • No reservation required for individual visitors.
    • Foreign visitors: please bring your passport.
  3. Entrance & security
    • Entrance: security checkpoint at the intersection of Baoqing Road and Bo'ai Road.
    • Security screening: queue in front of the Lixing Building.

Mountain

Yangmingshan (陽明山)

Park freeHalf a day

Volcanic hills, hot-spring valleys and misty trails just north of the city.

Getting there: MRT Red Line to Jiantan, then Bus 260 (about 40 minutes).

Tip: Cold, windy and often foggy in December. Bring a coat and check the forecast; swap days if it is pouring.

Open in Google Maps

Jiufen (九份)

Free to wanderHalf a day

A hillside old mining town with steep lantern-lit alleys, tea houses and snacks, and views of the sea.

Getting there: Bus 1062 from MRT Zhongxiao Fuxing, Exit 2 (about NT$90, 1–1.5 hours, every 15–30 minutes). Or train to Ruifang, then a short bus.

Tip: Buses get very crowded. Go in the afternoon to see the lanterns at dusk, and bring a rain jacket. Weekdays are quieter.

#Dessert · A Gab Yi Taro Ball 阿柑姨芋圓#TeaHouse · Jiufen Teahouse 九份茶坊

Elephant Mountain (象山)

Free1–1.5 hours round trip

A short, steep hike up stone steps to a rock ledge with the classic view of Taipei 101 and the city below.

Getting there: MRT Red Line to Xiangshan Station, Exit 2, then follow the signs to the trail (about 20–30 minutes up).

Tip: Go before sunset and bring a small flashlight for the way down. The steps are slippery when wet, so wear shoes with grip.

Street walk

Zhongshan & Chifeng Street (中山・赤峰街)

Free to wander3–4 hours

Zhongshan (中山): A stylish district of department stores, cafés, boutiques and a long linear park, popular with locals.

Chifeng Street (赤峰街): A lane of indie shops, vintage stores and small cafés tucked into an old neighborhood.

Getting there: MRT Red Line to Zhongshan Station. Chifeng Street is about 5–10 minutes on foot from Zhongshan or Shuanglian Station.

Tip: Chifeng shops usually open late morning. Check Google Maps before you go.

Taipei's youth-culture district: pedestrian streets packed with fashion, street snacks, arcades, cinemas and street performers, plus the historic Red House (西門紅樓).

Night markets

Raohe Street Night Market (饒河街觀光夜市)

Shilin Night Market (士林夜市)

Free entry

Taipei's largest. Fried chicken cutlets, big sausages, oyster omelet and a food court in the basement.

Getting there: MRT Red Line to Jiantan, Exit 1 (a few minutes on foot). Open from about 16:00 to midnight.

Open in Google Maps

Raohe Street Night Market (饒河街觀光夜市)

Free entry

One long street with a temple at the end. Try the pepper buns and herbal pork rib soup.

Getting there: MRT Green Line to Songshan, Exit 5. Open about 17:00–24:00. Start at the Songshan end.

Open in Google Maps

Ningxia Night Market (寧夏夜市)

Free entry

A compact, food-focused market in the old Datong district: taro balls, oyster omelet, fried chicken, braised dishes.

Getting there: MRT Red Line to Shuanglian, about 10 minutes on foot. Open from about 17:00. Go early for short lines.

Open in Google Maps

Night market culture

  • Night markets are a Taiwanese way of life: dinner, snacks and games in one place, usually from late afternoon until midnight.
  • Cash only at most stalls. Bring small bills and coins.
  • Most dishes cost NT$50–100, so share and try many small plates.
  • A long line usually means it is good.
  • Look for the stall's signature item on the banner.
  • Bins are rare. Eat near the stall and take your trash with you.

Food Guide

Taiwan is a food lover's paradise. Eat often, share plates and try everything.

Food culture

  • Eating is the national hobby. Meals are casual, quick and shared, and often cost under NT$200.
  • Convenience stores are everywhere and sell good hot food.
  • Many places hand you a paper menu to tick and give to staff.

Price guide: under NT$150   NT$150–500   over NT$500 per person.

Jamie's Corner

Jamie's Din Tai Fung Combo

At Din Tai Fung, the Taiwanese favorite is a fried rice plus a bowl of spicy wontons in chili oil (紅油抄手). Pour the chili oil sauce from the wontons over the fried rice. It is so delicious ~!

Jamie's order:

  • Original xiao long bao (原味小籠包)
  • Luffa and shrimp xiao long bao (絲瓜蝦仁小籠包)
  • Pork chop egg fried rice (排骨蛋炒飯)
  • Shrimp spicy wontons in chili oil (蝦肉紅油抄手)
  • Shaoxing drunken chicken (紹興醉雞)
  • Signature hot and sour soup (招牌酸辣湯)
  • Taro xiao long bao (芋泥小籠包)

Jamie's Corner

Jamie's Sweet Spot

I usually order light sugar (微糖, about 30%) with no ice (去冰). To me, it is just right!

微糖，去冰

Night market snacks (夜市小吃)

No single shops here, just the classics you will see at almost every night market.

Popcorn chicken (鹽酥雞)

Bite-size fried chicken tossed with white pepper, salt and fried basil. Add fried vegetables, tofu and sweet potato to the bag.

Recommended shop: 師園 (Shi Yuan). Google Maps

Gua bao (刈包)

Taiwan's "hamburger": a soft steamed bun folded around braised pork belly, pickled mustard greens, peanut powder and cilantro.

Recommended shop: 源芳刈包 (Yuan Fang Gua Bao). Google Maps

Sausage in sticky rice sausage (大腸包小腸)

A grilled Taiwanese sausage tucked inside a sticky-rice "sausage", with garlic, pickles and sweet sauce. Easy to eat while walking.

Oyster omelet (蚵仔煎)

Fresh oysters, egg, greens and sweet potato starch fried until chewy, then glazed with a sweet and savory red sauce.

Pig blood cake (米血糕)

Sticky rice cooked with pork blood, steamed, grilled on a stick and rolled in peanut powder and cilantro. It tastes like a savory, chewy rice cake, not like blood.

Stinky tofu (臭豆腐)

Fermented tofu, fried crisp or steamed, served with pickled cabbage. It smells strong but tastes much milder. Follow your nose to find a stall.

Fried sweet potato balls (地瓜球)

Chewy, hollow balls made from sweet potato dough, fried until crisp outside. Best eaten hot from the bag, and they come in several colors.

Scallion pancake with egg (炸彈蔥油餅)

A flaky scallion pancake fried with an egg inside, so it puffs up crisp outside and soft within. Often called a "bomb" pancake.

Suggested itineraries

Pick the themes you like and do them in any order.

Arrival night

Airport → Hotel
  • 21:00Land at TPE (flight CI762).
  • 21:45Immigration and baggage. Activate the eSIM and withdraw cash.
  • 22:15Taxi, Uber or a pre-booked car to the hotel (NT$1,100–1,500, about 50 minutes). The Airport MRT (NT$160 each, last trains roughly 22:40–23:35) only works if you travel light.
  • 23:15Check in and sleep.

Estimated: NT$1,100–1,500 for the car.

Jiufen at dusk

Hotel → Jiufen (private car) → 詹記麻辣火鍋 Dunnan
  • 11:00Leave the hotel by private car (about 1–1.5 hours to Jiufen).
  • 12:30Lunch and a slow walk along Jiufen Old Street: tea houses and the steep lantern-lit stairs.
  • 14:30Tea house break at Jiufen Teahouse (九份茶坊) or a sweet stop at A Gab Yi Taro Ball (阿柑姨芋圓).
  • 16:30Stay for dusk, when the lanterns light up. Sunset is around 17:00 in December.
  • 17:00Car back to Taipei.
  • 18:30Hot pot dinner at 詹記麻辣火鍋 (Dunnan branch).
  • 20:00Back to the hotel.

Estimated: 8-hour charter NT$4,600 for 7 people (about NT$657 each), plus food.

Wellness trip

Hotel → 陽明山水溫泉會館 (Jinshan) → lunch → Shilin Night Market → hotel
  • 09:30Leave the hotel by private car or taxi (allow over an hour to Jinshan).
  • 11:00Arrive and take a private hot spring room (湯屋).
  • 13:00Lunch at the resort (check its dining options and hours first).
  • 14:30Rest, a short walk and a second soak if you like.
  • 15:30Head back to Taipei.
  • 18:00Evening at Shilin Night Market: dinner and snacks, then a short walk through the stalls.
  • 20:30Back to the hotel.

Estimated: private room NT$800 (weekdays) or NT$1,000 (weekends and holidays) for 1 hour and 2 people, +NT$400 per extra adult, plus transport and night market food.

Hot spring: 陽明山水溫泉會館

Open in Google Maps   Official price page

  • Public hot spring pool (大眾湯): NT$500 per adult on weekdays, NT$600 on weekends and holidays (list price NT$800). Children 140 cm and under: NT$200. No time limit.
  • Private hot spring room (湯屋): 1 hour for two people, NT$800 on weekdays, NT$1,000 on weekends and holidays. Each extra adult adds NT$400.
  • Sat, Dec 26 should be charged the weekend rate. Please confirm on arrival.
  • Lunch is planned at the resort. Please check its dining menu and hours in advance.
  • The outdoor pool areas require a swimsuit and swim cap. The nude baths (裸湯) are separated by gender.
  • The address is 新北市金山區重和里林口33-3號 in Jinshan District, at the foot of Yangmingshan. It is a separate spot from the main park, so check the route on Google Maps or take a taxi.

Prices are from the resort's official price page and may change. Opening hours were not listed there, so check before you go.

Culture trip

Presidential Office Building → Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall → Chun Shui Tang → dinner
  • 09:00Presidential Office Building (free, Mon–Fri 09:00–12:00, last entry 11:30). Bring your passport and expect a security check.
  • 11:15Arrive at Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall and plan about 2 hours here. Climb the steps and walk the plaza and gardens.
  • 12:00Lunch and milk tea at Chun Shui Tang (春水堂), right at the memorial hall.
  • 13:00Watch the changing of the guard (on the hour), then head back to the hotel to rest.
  • 17:30Dinner at Psalms Cafe & Restaurant.
  • 19:00Back to the hotel.

Estimated: about NT$1,000 per person including meals.

City icons

Hotel → Taipei 101 → Din Tai Fung → 18 Guanjun Beef Noodle Restaurant
  • 10:00Taipei 101 mall: elevators and wide aisles. Coffee at Simple Kaffa.
  • 11:30Early lunch at Din Tai Fung (Taipei 101 branch). Take a queue number as soon as you arrive.
  • 13:00Browse around Taipei 101 after lunch: shops, a coffee break, and the observatory (NT$600–650, book online) if you like.
  • 17:30Early evening dinner at 18 Guanjun Beef Noodle Restaurant (18號冠軍牛肉麵).
  • 19:00Back to the hotel.

Estimated: about NT$1,600 per person.

Old Taipei & treats

Breakfast → Zhongshan & Chifeng → nap → Dihua Street
  • 08:30Taiwanese breakfast at 好初早餐 (Zhongshan).
  • 10:00Zhongshan and Chifeng Street: flat streets, shops and cafés. Coffee at Ge Leisi Cafe or dessert at 榕美術館.
  • 12:00Lu rou fan lunch.
  • 13:00Back to the hotel for a nap.
  • 15:30Dihua Street: tea, dried goods and souvenirs. Try Lin’s Wagashi Confectionery or the oyster fritters at 蔡記.
  • 19:00Back to the hotel to pack and rest.

Estimated: about NT$1,500 per person.
